- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.8) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, cap peak forecast at 1.5x recent high or 20% below true peak.
- In low sentiment (≤0.4) periods, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for mean reversion toward historical mean.
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% for 3+ consecutive days, adjust future forecasts downward by 0.5–1.0% per day until sentiment shifts.
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast mean is 2–3% below true mean over last 5 forecasts, apply upward bias correction of 0.5–1.0% to next forecast.
- When sentiment swings from positive to negative, model often lags; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days and apply downward bias only after sentiment confirms negative trend.
